problem: Source lists three qualities of the estranged relatives: "far-distant, long-absent, wholly estranged". MODERN keeps only "long separated and wholly estranged"; the physical distance ("far-distant") is dropped.
new_text: Premonitions are strange things! And so are sympathies; and so are signs; and the three combined form one mystery to which humanity has not yet found the key. I never laughed at premonitions in my life, because I have had strange ones of my own. Sympathies, I believe, exist—for instance, between relatives far apart, long separated and wholly estranged, who still assert, despite their alienation, the bond of their common origin—and their workings baffle human understanding. And signs, for all we know, may be nothing but Nature's sympathy with humanity.

problem: Rochester echoes Jane's own phrase from 21.37 ("his wife cast me off"): source "besides, you say she cast you off." MODERN "threw you out" changes the sense (Mrs. Reed disowned Jane and sent her to school; she did not evict her) and loses the echo, which 21.37 MODERN keeps as "cast me off".
new_text: "And what good can you do her? Nonsense, Jane! I would never think of travelling a hundred miles to see an old lady who will perhaps be dead before you arrive—and besides, you say she cast you off."

problem: Source "I suppose I do come on" answers Rochester's "Come on, if you please" (22.17, MODERN "Come here"). MODERN "I suppose I do go" is ambiguous on first reading (go away? go to him?) and breaks the answer to his summons.
new_text: I suppose I do come forward; though in what manner I cannot tell, since I am barely conscious of my movements, concerned only with appearing calm and, above all, with controlling the muscles of my face—which I feel rebelling against my will, struggling to express what I had resolved to hide. But I have a veil—it is down. I may still manage to behave with some composure.
